<action type="say">
Amtrak app bookings won’t show up in this system, so we have to track it down on Amtrak’s side.

Try this, in order:

1) Check the Amtrak app  
- Open the Amtrak app on the same phone you used.  
- Make sure you’re signed into the same Amtrak account (same email) you usually use.  
- Tap “Trips” or “My Trips”:  
  - If it was booked while signed in, your NE Regional BOS → WAS trip for October should appear there.  
  - If it doesn’t, you may have checked out as a guest or the purchase never completed.

2) Look for the Amtrak confirmation email  
Search your email (all folders, including spam) for:  
- “Amtrak”, “eTicket”, “Reservation Confirmation”  
- Or the last 4 digits of the card you would’ve used  
Every Amtrak ticket generates an email with a 6‑character reservation code (like “A1BC23”). If there’s no Amtrak email at all, that’s a strong sign the booking didn’t finish.

3) Check your card/bank statement  
Look for a charge from “AMTRAK” around the day you think you booked.  
- Charge present + no email/app trip → contact Amtrak with the card details and your name; they can pull the reservation.  
- No charge → the booking almost certainly never ticketed.

If you’d like, tell me:
- Rough day you tried to book, and  
- The card brand you used (e.g., Chase Visa, Amex)  
and I’ll give you a precise “what to look for” on the statement and suggest the exact info to have ready if you call Amtrak. If you confirm there’s no charge and no email, you’ll want to just rebook the NE Regional for your October dates.</action>

Given you’re not sure of the date or card, the goal is to do a one‑time, thorough check so you don’t keep wondering.

Do this in order:

1) Amtrak account (most important)  
- On your phone, open the Amtrak app.  
- Confirm which email it shows under “Account” or “Profile.”  
- Then, on a computer/phone browser, go to amtrak.com and sign in with that same email.  
- Check “My Trips” / “Upcoming Trips.”  
If the NE Regional BOS–DC trip doesn’t appear there, it’s very likely it never completed (unless you definitely checked out as a guest).

2) Email search (all accounts)  
For each email you actually use, search “Amtrak” and “eTicket”:  
- No Amtrak emails at all in the last few months → extremely likely no ticket was issued.  
You don’t need the exact date; just scan anything from Amtrak since, say, June.

3) Wallet & travel apps  
- Open Apple Wallet / Google Wallet / any travel app you use (TripIt, Google Trips, etc.) and see if an Amtrak ticket is stored there.  
If nothing shows up plus no email plus no trip in your Amtrak account, you can safely assume the booking never finished.

4) Card checks (optional but conclusive)  
If you want to be 100% sure, quickly scan recent transactions on each card you commonly use:  
- Look for “AMTRAK” or similar merchant name any time in the last 1–2 months.  
- If you do see an Amtrak charge but still don’t see the trip, that’s when you call Amtrak and give them:  
  - Your name (Kevin O’Brien / OBrien / O Brien variants)  
  - Approx dates (around Oct 10–14) and route (Boston to DC)  
  - Last 4 digits of the card and approximate charge amount  
They can pull your reservation by payment info.
